title: PR #11 — Auth rate limiting, lockout, and admin user management
description: Protect authentication endpoints from brute force, add account lockout, and give the first admin a panel to create, disable, and re-session users without email delivery. Requirement IDs: TASK-24, TASK-25.
acceptanceCriteria: `/auth/login`, `/auth/2fa`, `/auth/recover`, and `/setup` are rate limited per IP hash and per email via the Workers Rate Limiting binding
Requests over the limit return 429 with a `Retry-After` header
Ten consecutive failed password attempts lock the account for 15 minutes and return 423 with `Retry-After`
One account's lockout does not consume another account's per-email budget
Admin can list users, create a user, disable/enable a user, and revoke sessions
Creating a user returns a one-time 24-hour setup token that the admin copies manually; no email is sent
A disabled user cannot log in and all existing sessions are rejected
The last active admin cannot be disabled or demoted
Every admin mutation emits an audit event

steps.details: Create `app/lib/.server/rate-limit.ts` using `env.RATE_LIMITER.limit({ key })` with keys such as `login:ip:<hash>` and `login:email:<hash>`. Hash IPs and emails with HMAC-SHA256 using `AUTH_PEPPER` so raw identifiers are never stored. Apply to the auth routes listed in the acceptance criteria and return 429 with `Retry-After` when `success` is false.

On failed password verification, atomically update `failed_login_count = failed_login_count + 1` and set `locked_until` when the count reaches 10. On success, reset both. Check `locked_until` before verifying the hash and return 423 with the remaining seconds. Use a conditional update so concurrent attempts cannot bypass the threshold.

steps.description: Add the admin guard and routes
steps.details: Create `requireAdmin(request, env)` that calls `requireUser` and checks `role === 'admin'`, returning 403 otherwise. Add `app/routes/admin.users.tsx` with a loader listing id, email, role, status, created_at, and 2FA enabled, and actions for create, disable, enable, and revoke.

Create a `setup_invitations` D1 table with a hashed 24-hour token, email, display name, role, inviter, and consumed marker. Admin create inserts only the invitation and returns `APP_ORIGIN/setup/member?token=...`. The member route derives keys locally and atomically consumes the invitation and creates the user; the admin never sees secrets. Token is single-use.

Disabling a user sets `status='disabled'` and increments the session version so all sessions fail the guard. Enabling restores login but not sessions. Ensure `requireUser` rejects disabled users for both pages and API routes.
Before disabling or demoting, count active admins inside the same D1 batch as the update. Abort with 409 when the count would drop to zero.

Add the users UI in `app/features/admin-users/` (page entry, components, hooks); the route module stays transport-only. Include status badges, a create dialog, and row actions (disable/enable, revoke sessions). Show the setup link in a copyable, one-time panel with an explicit warning that it expires in 24 hours. No email field is sent anywhere.

Vitest: 11th attempt returns 429; 10th failure sets `locked_until`; successful login resets counters; disabling the last admin returns 409; setup token works once and then 401. Playwright: admin creates a member, member completes setup in a separate context, admin disables them, member is logged out.

technicalNotes: The rate limiting binding is approximate and edge-local; account lockout in D1 is the authoritative protection.
Never persist raw IPs or emails for rate limiting; store HMACs.
Setup invitations belong in D1 so consume-and-create is atomic; KV cannot atomically consume a token.
Admin actions must not expose another user's ciphertext or wrapped keys in the list response.
Audit events are defined in TASK-19; emit through a small interface now and let TASK-19 implement storage if it has not merged.
